13th 1950
Mein Allerliebstes,

Du weißt gar nicht, wie es mir
gelungen hat
so von dir wegzufahren zu sein. Aber
manches Mal
geht es mit mir durch. Glücklicherweise
wird es immer seltener.
Ich habe mich so sehr mit Feines
fein am Telefon gefreut. Hoffe
wenig beunruhigt. Es
habe ich dich ein wenig
absolute
ist immer dasselbe
"nichts", hier ist was sich beim
Arzt abgespielt hat.

Er war außergewöhnlich nett. Ich
habe versucht ihm alles so objektiv
als möglich zu erklären. Abgesehen
davon dass ich mich schon wieder
"ganz normal" gefühlt habe, hat
er natürlich weiter beruhigt und auch
mich gewirkt, sodass ich mich empfand,
wie nach der ersten Visite mit Dir
bei ihm fühlte.

Lediglich Perl meint er, dass es ganz
falsch ist von diesen Dingen wegzulaufen
im Gegenteil man soll sich
daran

morgen

translated_text: July 13, 1950 My dearest, you have no idea how I managed to get so far away from you. But sometimes I just get carried away. Fortunately, it's happening less and less often. I was so happy to talk to Feines on the phone. I hope you weren't too worried. I've been a little bit... Absolutely, it's always the same "nothing." Here's what happened at the doctor's. He was exceptionally kind. I tried to explain everything to him as objectively as possible. Apart from the fact that I already felt "completely normal" again, he naturally continued to reassure me and had the same effect on me, so that I felt like I did after the first visit with you. He only said that it's completely wrong to run away from these things; on the contrary, one should get used to them, because perhaps tomorrow someone else will tell me the same thing. It's much better to face them and deal with them on your own, even if it impresses you a lot at first. I think he's right. Anyway, that's the main thing, it's reassuring. I'll probably get your letter tomorrow. I don't need to tell you how much I'm looking forward to it. On Thursday, Ersi and I will be at the Randvers, which sends its warmest greetings to everyone. It's in Atlantic City, and Ersi and I are excited to see the new place and think of my little one. Give us kisses, the children, and everyone else. It's only two more days until I can hug you again. Lots of love from your Betty. NEW YORK NY JUL 11 2 10:30 AM 1950 CATHEDRAL STATION UNITED STATES POSTAGE Mrs. Rob. Zentall c/o James Rose Spruceton NY near Westhill NY 3 CENTS
